workstream.name: ecl v1 — the real interpreter (design/workstream-v1.md)
workstream.unlocks: Milestone 3 (frame-machine first light) executes reader output; the print∘parse round-trip law becomes enforceable; every later milestone's fixtures are written in ecl source instead of hand-built values.

problemStatement: The value layer (Milestone 1, landed at commit 8295fd5 and green through all CI gates including instrumented Linux TSan) can represent every ecl value but nothing can produce values from source text. GRAMMAR.md is fully specified and proven by the poc reader, yet the Zig implementation has no reader: no tokens, no forms, no spans, no binder lowering, no REPL continuation detection. Milestone 3's frame machine cannot exist without reader output to execute.
solutionSummary: Implement the GRAMMAR.md reader over the landed value layer in five patches: a lexer (cursor, spans, comments/comma-whitespace, whole-token number classification including inf/hex/underscores, diagnostics); the form parser (matched pairs, strings/chars/symbols/words with interning, dict-literal desugar to `( body ) dict-of`, code-plane span side tables keyed by list identity, REPL Complete/Incomplete status); binder lowering to point-free code with the boundary-crossing error; extraction of M1's seeded value generator into a shared test helper; and the round-trip law — parse(print(v)) reproduces v exactly for dict-free values, with dict desugaring asserted separately (structural identity for dicts closes at M3 when dict-of can evaluate). All poc reader fixtures are ported as regression anchors.
currentStateAnalysis: Verified against HEAD (2dadc3c): src/ contains the complete M1 value layer — value.zig (16-byte Value, frozen HeapKind), heap.zig (atomic RC, isUnique, releaseValue), intern.zig (intern/get, u32 ids), list.zig (fromValues with construction specialization, fromValuesGeneric, fromCodepoints, at, len), equal.zig (match/hash with exact int-float comparison), dict.zig (fromPairs/get/put/del/merge), print.zig (print/toOwnedString, GRAMMAR escapes, poc parity fixtures), value_test.zig (seeded generateValue/generateList/generateDict — currently test-file-private, to be extracted for reuse). There is no lexer, reader, binder, or span machinery in Zig. The authoritative predecessor is poc/rust/src/reader.rs (745 lines: Parser with line/col spans, ReadStatus Complete/Incomplete, classify_number/classify_inf, escape handling, dict desugar emitting two forms, lower_binder emitting `[] cons` + `dup <i> at swap` + `(form) dip` + `pop`, nested-binder-name rejection). CI runs six blocking tasks (ZLint was promoted from advisory to blocking --deny-warnings after M1 landed — .builds/ci.yml `lint` task), so all new code must be warning-clean under ZLint v0.9.1 as well as fmt/Debug/ReleaseSafe/TSan.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: Not applicable: this gameplan adds no external dependency. CI continues on the existing builds.sr.ht manifest; no manifest changes are needed (the reader adds no packages, and ZLint v0.9.1 is already pinned and blocking).
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The load-bearing intra-project contract this gameplan creates is the reader's output shape consumed by Milestone 3: `Parsed { forms: []Value, spans: SpanTable, source_name }` with `SpanTable` keyed by code-list identity (*Header) and element index, plus the `ReadResult` Complete/Incomplete split for REPL continuation. M3's frame machine walks `forms` and reads `spans` at unwind time to build d.19 error dicts. The shape is named once in src/reader.zig and documented as the M3 handoff; changing it later is a design event. Provenance semantics follow d.23: spans exist only for reader-built lists — code assembled at runtime has none (absence-is-absence), and identity-keyed spans are naturally dropped on CoW copy.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: Two failure classes. (1) Malformed source: every lexical/structural error returns error.Parse with a Diag {message, line, col} written through the read() diagnostic out-parameter (never a panic, never a partial Parsed); incomplete input (unclosed delimiter/string/binder) is NOT an error — it returns ReadResult.incomplete so the REPL can continue the line, exactly poc's ReadStatus split. (2) OutOfMemory propagates from every allocating path per the M1 policy; a failing read releases every value it built (checkAllAllocationFailures sweeps the full read path in Patch 5). Oversized inputs: int literals outside i64 and floats outside f64 are parse errors with the literal in the message (poc parity); form nesting uses an explicit heap context stack capped at 10,000, so pathological input returns a parse diagnostic without consuming the host stack.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: The reader is per-invocation sequential state (a Parser struct over one source buffer); no shared mutable state except interning words/symbols through the global intern table, whose thread-safety M1 established and TSan-tests. Reading the same source twice yields structurally `match`-equal forms and equal span tables (reader is deterministic); interned ids are stable within a process, so repeated reads are idempotent in the only sense the language defines.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: Not applicable: no persistent state, no migrations, no manifest changes. Reverting the gameplan's patches restores the repo exactly.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: Ungated (option 3: no flag), same rationale as value-core: the reader is a library layer with no user-reachable surface until Milestone 3 wires the CLI; the repo has no flag infrastructure and nothing to gate.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Two tracks. Main chain (1→2→3→5): lexer → forms → binder → round-trip suite, serialized because each consumes the previous layer and patches 1/2/3/5 all append exports to src/root.zig (the shared frame). Side track (4): the test-generator extraction touches only src/value_test.zig + src/testgen.zig and runs parallel to the chain; patch 5 joins both tracks.

functionalChanges.description: Number tokens classify whole-token per GRAMMAR.md: decimal with `_` separators, `0x` hex, floats requiring digits on both sides of the dot with optional exponent, `inf`/`+inf`/`-inf` as float literals, `-3` a literal while `-` and `2dup` stay words; out-of-range literals are parse errors naming the literal.

Source text parses to value-layer forms per GRAMMAR.md: matched `()`/`[]` pairs (mismatch is a parse error with line/col), `'name` quoted symbols with dotted-qualification validation, strings and chars with the full escape set, comma-as-whitespace, `#` comments, and reserved `;`/`|` errors — with every reader-built list carrying spans in the code-plane side table.
Dict literals desugar at read time to the two forms `( body )` `dict-of`, including nested literals; `{}` yields the empty-body pair.
An all-char quotation like `(\a \b)` reads as the identical value to `"ab"` (construction specialization applies to reader-built lists).
Interactive input is classified Complete or Incomplete: unclosed delimiters, strings, and binders report incomplete-with-span (REPL continuation) instead of erroring.

Head-position binders lower to point-free code at read time — the stored list contains cons/dup/at/swap/dip/pop words and no binder names; duplicate names, empty binders, qualified/numeric names, and locals crossing a quotation boundary are parse errors (the last suggesting `cons`).

The round-trip law holds and is enforced in CI: for seeded dict-free values, parse(print(v)) yields exactly one form that `match`es v with equal hash; for dicts, parse(print(d)) yields the desugared pair whose body list interleaves d's keys and values in insertion order.

contextResources.why: The normative grammar: source/token/form rules, reserved characters, binder syntax and bind order, unit boundaries, and the round-trip closure this milestone enforces. Every lexer and parser decision resolves against this document.

The proven predecessor implementation: Parser cursor with line/col bumping, ReadStatus Complete/Incomplete, classify_number/classify_inf ordering, escape handling, dict desugar emitting exactly two forms, lower_binder's emission scheme ([] cons per name; dup <index> at swap per reference; (form) dip per ordinary form; trailing pop), and nested-local rejection. Its test fixtures are the porting source for Patch 5.

The landed substrate the reader builds on: list.fromValues (construction specialization — reader-built all-char lists become char leaves), intern.intern for word/symbol ids, Value union shapes, heap.releaseValue/retainValue ownership discipline for error-path cleanup. Signatures must be consumed exactly as they exist on disk.

The other half of the round-trip law: the printer's canonical spellings (char \u{...} escaping of reserved characters, float trailing-.0, inf/-inf, dict {k v} rendering) define exactly what the reader must re-read. toOwnedString is the fuzz harness's serialization.

Decision 23's provenance rules (reader-plane spans in side tables keyed by list identity; runtime values carry none; absence-is-absence for runtime-built code) and ARCHITECTURE.md §Boundary layers — the span-table design implements these and M3 consumes them for error dicts.

The seeded generators being extracted (generateValue/generateList/generateDict, randomCodepoint, randomInternedId) — Patch 4 moves them verbatim into testgen.zig and re-points value_test.zig, preserving seeds and distributions so M1's property suite is unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: All six CI gates pass: zig fmt --check, zig build test (Debug), -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe, zig build test-tsan (instrumented on Linux), and ZLint v0.9.1 --deny-warnings.

Every GRAMMAR.md token rule has a passing fixture: comma-whitespace, # comments, `_` separators, 0x hex, inf/+inf/-inf, whole-token discipline (`2dup`/`1+` are words, `-3` is a literal), digits-both-sides floats, out-of-range int/float parse errors.

Every GRAMMAR.md form rule has a passing fixture: matched-pair enforcement (`[1 2)` errors with line/col), dict desugar to `( body ) dict-of` including nesting and `{}`, string/char escape round-trips including \u{...}, quoted and dotted symbols with leading/trailing/double-dot rejection, reserved `;` and `|` errors.

Binder fixtures pass: `(|x| x x *)` lowers to the poc-canonical point-free list (asserted via its printed form), bind order leftmost-deepest, duplicate/empty/invalid names error, and `(|x| (x))` errors suggesting cons.
ReadResult classifies `1 (2` as incomplete (with span) and `1 (2]` as a parse error — the REPL continuation split.

The round-trip property runs ≥1000 seeded cases in CI: dict-free parse(print(v)) yields exactly one form matching v with equal hash; dict desugar-shape assertions cover dict-containing values; full structural dict round-trip is explicitly deferred to M3 (needs dict-of evaluation) and documented in the test.
Reader-built lists have spans for every element in the SpanTable, keyed by list identity, with source name, line, and col; values built by hand have none (absence-is-absence probe).
checkAllAllocationFailures sweeps the full read path (lexing, form building, binder lowering, span-table population) with zero leaks on every failure point.
value_test.zig's property suite is byte-for-byte behavior-identical after the generator extraction (same seeds, same distributions, all M1 tests green).
src/ stays inside the d.23 core budget; the embedded line-budget test is extended to count the new modules.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The round-trip law at M2 is scoped to dict-free values, with dict desugar-shape assertions as the dict-side check; full dict round-trip closes at M3.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Dict literals desugar at read time (d.17), so parse(print(dict)) yields `( body ) dict-of` — two forms, not a dict value. Structural identity for dicts requires evaluating dict-of, which needs M3's machine. Asserting the desugared shape (body interleaves keys/values in insertion order) is the complete reader-level obligation; anything stronger would misstate the grammar.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Spans live in a per-Parsed side table keyed by (*Header, element index), owned by Parsed and freed with it; the M3 machine holds Parsed alive for code it executes.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Implements d.23 exactly: provenance on the code plane, never on values; identity-keyed spans naturally die when code is CoW-copied or built at runtime (absence-is-absence). A parallel token-stream table was considered and rejected — the frame machine unwinds via (list, index) pairs, so identity+index is the shape M3's lazy trace builder consumes directly.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Form nesting uses an explicit context stack capped at 10,000 open containers.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The first implementation followed the planned recursive descent, but an adversarial 10,001-open-form probe exhausted the host stack before the nominal guard. The explicit context stack makes the promised 'form nesting too deep' diagnostic real, retains simple scalar parsing, and enforces the no-host-crash doctrine empirically.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The lexer and parser are separate modules (lexer.zig owns tokens/spans/diagnostics; reader.zig owns forms), and binder lowering is its own module.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Keeps the patch frames disjoint and reviewable, and gives M3 a clean import for Diag/Span types without pulling the whole parser. poc's single-file layout was fine at proof scale; the real implementation separates the layers the gameplan patches touch independently.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Patch 4 extracts M1's generators instead of duplicating them in reader_test.zig.
explicitOpinions.rationale: One generator = one distribution: the round-trip law should fuzz the same value space M1's equality/hash laws fuzz, so a divergence between suites can't hide a gap. The extraction is behavior-preserving (same seeds) and value_test.zig keeps its assertions unchanged.

explicitOpinions.opinion: ZLint's promotion to a blocking --deny-warnings gate (made after M1 landed) is inherited as-is; all new modules must be warning-clean.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The user promoted the linter in .builds/ci.yml; this gameplan treats it as part of the strictness harness rather than re-litigating it. The workstream's strictness decision text is updated in the write-back.

patches.title: Lexer: cursor, spans, diagnostics, whole-token classification

files.description: Span {line: u32, col: u32}; Diag {message: []const u8 (static or fixed-buffer), span: Span}; Cursor over []const u8 with peek/peekN/bump maintaining line/col (newline resets col); skipIgnored (Unicode whitespace + comma + # comments); isTokenBoundary per GRAMMAR (whitespace, comma, the six delimiters, '"', '#'); takeToken with reserved-char stops (';', '|', '\'', '\\'); classify(token) → union(enum){ int: i64, float: f64, word, out_of_range } implementing whole-token number discipline: optional sign; decimal digits with `_` between digits; 0x hex with i64 range checks (including -0x8000000000000000); floats digits-both-sides-of-dot with optional e/E exponent, finite-only; inf/+inf/-inf as float literals; everything else word.
Export pub const lexer; add test aggregation.

changes: Port poc's classify_number/classify_inf/looks_like_number logic (poc/rust/src/reader.rs) to a single classify() with the identical acceptance set, keeping the out-of-range arm distinct so the parser can produce the poc-parity error message naming the literal.
Track spans at token start: span() captures (line, col) before takeToken, matching poc's provenance points so ported fixtures agree on positions.
Diagnostics: a Diag slot filled before returning error.Parse; messages are comptime string literals or formatted into a caller-provided fixed buffer — no allocation on the error path.

Every switch over classification results is else-less; tests cover the full GRAMMAR token matrix including `2dup`, `1+`, `-`, `-3`, `1_000_000`, `0x10`; `.5` and `5.` are parse errors, full stop (not numbers by the digits-both-sides rule, then invalid symbols by the leading/trailing-dot rules); `9223372036854775808` out-of-range.

patches.spec:
module READER_PATCH_1.

> Whole-token classification is total: every token is exactly one of
> int, float, word, or an out-of-range diagnostic (GRAMMAR.md tokens).

Token.
Classification.
int-c => Classification.
float-c => Classification.
word-c => Classification.
range-c => Classification.
classify t: Token => Classification.
numeric-shape? t: Token => Bool.
---
> Tokens without a complete numeric shape are words — `2dup` and `1+`
> classify as words, never as errors.
all t: Token, ~(numeric-shape? t) | classify t = word-c.

> Classification is deterministic.
all t: Token | classify t = classify t.

patches.title: Form parser: matched pairs, dict desugar, spans, REPL status

files.description: ReadResult = union(enum){ complete: Parsed, incomplete: Incomplete }; Parsed { forms: []Value, spans: SpanTable, source_name: []const u8, deinit() }; SpanTable = std.AutoHashMapUnmanaged(*value.Header, []lexer.Span) plus a top-level forms span slice; Incomplete { message, span }; read(allocator, source_name, source, diag) drives lexer tokens through scalar parsing plus an explicit container-context stack: lists with matched pairs, dict desugar to two forms, strings with escapes (\\ \" \n \t \u{...}), chars (\a, \space/\tab/\newline, \u{...}, single boundary chars), quoted symbols with dot validation, and words interned via intern.intern; all list construction flows through the M1 list APIs; error paths release every built value.
Export pub const reader; add test aggregation.

changes: Implement read() per GRAMMAR.md forms: program = form*; unmatched closers and cross-pair mismatches are parse errors with the opener's span in the message (poc message shapes preserved for fixture parity); EOF inside a delimiter/string returns ReadResult.incomplete.
Dict desugar exactly as poc: `{ body }` produces the body list (with spans) followed by the interned `dict-of` word carrying the literal's span — nested literals desugar inside their enclosing body.

Span discipline (d.23): as each list closes, record a []Span parallel to its elements under the list's *Header in SpanTable; top-level forms get their own span slice; spans are recorded for the list the reader BUILT — after construction specialization the header registered is whatever fromValues returned (char leaves included).

Ownership: Parsed owns one reference to each top-level form and frees the span slices and table in deinit; any parse failure after partial construction walks already-built forms with heap.releaseValue (checkAllAllocationFailures in Patch 5 proves leak-freedom).

Depth guard: an explicit container-context stack capped at 10_000 converts deeper input into error.Parse ('form nesting too deep'); the 10,001-open-form regression proves host-stack exhaustion is not reachable from source nesting.

precedents.name: PEP 657 — fine-grained error locations in side tables on code objects
precedents.whyApplicable: The span-table design implemented here: per-element source positions stored beside the code object (keyed by list identity + index), decoded only when a trace is rendered — never carried on runtime values. M3's lazy trace builder consumes exactly this shape.

patches.title: Binder lowering to point-free code

files.description: lower(allocator, names, body, diag) implementing poc's emission scheme with interned word ids: empty-list literal then one `cons` per name (leftmost name = deepest value); for each body form — a name reference becomes `dup <index> at swap`, any other form becomes `( form )` `dip`; trailing `pop`. Validation: names must be unquoted, unqualified, non-numeric, distinct; empty binder rejected; nested list/dict forms containing a binder name are rejected with the 'crosses a quotation boundary; capture it explicitly with `cons`' diagnostic (iterative worklist scan over body forms).

Wire the binder hook: after an opener, a `|` token parses the name list (second `|` closes it; EOF is incomplete) and routes the parsed body through binder.lower before list construction; `|` anywhere else stays a parse error.
Export pub const binder; add test aggregation.

changes: Intern the six lowering words (cons, dup, at, swap, dip, pop) once at lower() entry; emitted forms carry the binder's span in the span table (generated code traces to the binder site).
Port poc's lower_binder emission order exactly so the canonical fixture holds: `(|x| x x *)` prints as `([] cons dup 0 at swap dup 0 at swap (*) dip pop)`.
Boundary-crossing scan walks nested lists and desugared dict bodies (a dict literal inside a binder body is a quotation boundary too, per d.17).
Fixtures: bind order (`10 20 (|lo hi| …)` shape — asserted structurally on the lowered list since execution arrives at M3), duplicate/empty/invalid names, `(|x| (x))` error text.
patches.spec:
module READER_PATCH_3.

> Binder lowering erases names before storage (d.6): the stored list is
> point-free and contains no binder name.

Name.
Form.
Lowered.
lower ns: [Name], body: [Form] => Lowered.
contains-name? l: Lowered, n: Name => Bool.
valid-names? ns: [Name] => Bool.
crosses-boundary? ns: [Name], body: [Form] => Bool.
lower-ok? ns: [Name], body: [Form] => Bool.
---
> Lowering succeeds exactly when names are valid and no name crosses a
> quotation boundary.
all ns: [Name], body: [Form] | lower-ok? ns body = (valid-names? ns and ~(crosses-boundary? ns body)).

> The lowered list never mentions a binder name.
all ns: [Name], body: [Form], n: Name, lower-ok? ns body | ~(contains-name? (lower ns body) n).

precedents.name: Brent Kerby — The Theory of Concatenative Combinators (2002)
precedents.whyApplicable: The reference for eliminating named values into dip/dup/swap combinator sequences — the theory behind poc's emission scheme this patch ports. Useful when validating that the protected-locals-list lowering is a faithful abstraction algorithm rather than an ad-hoc translation.

patches.title: Round-trip law, poc fixture port, and read-path OOM sweep

files.description: The cross-layer suite: (1) round-trip law — ≥1000 seeded dict-free values via testgen: print via print.toOwnedString, read back, assert exactly one form, equal.match with the original, equal hash; (2) dict desugar shape — for seeded dicts, parse(print(d)) yields [body-list, dict-of word] with body elements matching keys/values interleaved in insertion order (documented note: structural dict round-trip closes at M3); (3) ported poc reader fixtures (atoms/comments/commas, unicode escapes, dict two-forms with canonical prints, binder canonical lowering, incomplete continuation, mismatched delimiters, out-of-range int); (4) checkAllAllocationFailures over a read() covering every construct (nested lists, dict literal, binder, string, all number forms); (5) extend the embedded line-budget test to include lexer/reader/binder/testgen/reader_test sources.

The line-budget test's @embedFile list gains the five new sources (budget assertion thresholds unchanged: core < 2000 was M1's headroom — raise the core bound to 3500 to cover the reader layer while staying inside d.23's ~5k, and assert it explicitly).

changes: The round-trip property is the milestone's teeth: any printer spelling the reader cannot re-read (or vice versa) fails CI here — this is the d.16 closure at last enforced by machine.

Fixture parity: poc's expected strings are copied as literals (e.g. lowering canonical form, '(\a 'x "ok")' from the mixed-list fixture) so both implementations are pinned to the same observable outputs.
OOM sweep drives read() through checkAllAllocationFailures with a source exercising every allocation site (span slices, table entries, binder emission, string building).
Line-budget: update the embedded audit; log core and total counts as in M1.

crosses-boundary? ns: [Name], body: [Form] => Bool.
lower-ok? ns: [Name], body: [Form] => Bool.

dict-free? v: Value => Bool.
print v: Value => Str.
parse s: Str => Value.
match? a: Value, b: Value => Bool.
hash v: Value => Nat0.
---
> Token classification is total and deterministic; incomplete numeric
> shapes are words.
all t: Token, ~(numeric-shape? t) | classify t = word-c.
all t: Token | classify t = classify t.

> Reading is total (complete, incomplete, or diagnostic) and
> deterministic.
all s: Source | read s = read s.

> Code-plane provenance: every reader-built list carries one span per
> element; nothing else does (d.23 absence-is-absence).
all l: CodeList, reader-built? l | #(spans-of l) = elements-of l.

> Binder erasure: lowering succeeds iff names are valid and stay inside
> the quotation; the stored list never mentions a binder name.
all ns: [Name], body: [Form] | lower-ok? ns body = (valid-names? ns and ~(crosses-boundary? ns body)).
all ns: [Name], body: [Form], n: Name, lower-ok? ns body | ~(contains-name? (lower ns body) n).

> The grammar is closed under printing for dict-free values.
all v: Value, dict-free? v | match? (parse (print v)) v.
all v: Value, dict-free? v | hash (parse (print v)) = hash v.
